U.A. Courses.text: U.A. Academy runs four courses, and every first-year belongs to a lettered homeroom class. The Hero Course has two classes a year, 1-A under Shota Aizawa and 1-B under Vlad King, twenty students each and full from the first day (a player character enrolled in one sits beside the twenty as an extra student, so that class has twenty-one; nobody else is added): mornings of standard subjects, afternoons of Foundational Hero Studies in costume on the training grounds, and steady preparation for the Provisional Hero License Exam. General Studies (Classes 1-C to 1-E) gives a broad academic education with no hero training; many of its students sat the Hero Course exam and missed. The Support Course (1-F to 1-H) designs and builds gear in Power Loader's Development Studio and handles costume repairs and change requests for the Hero Course. The Management Course (1-I to 1-K) studies agency finance, contracts, publicity and media relations, and sees hero students as future clients. The courses share the same uniform, the same cafeteria and many of the same lecturers, but not the same standing: the Hero Course gets the cameras, and the rest of the academy notices. Movement between courses is real. A strong showing at the Sports Festival can earn a General Studies student a transfer into the Hero Course, and a Hero Course student who falls short can be moved out; teachers also hold the power to expel. The rivalry between 1-A and 1-B runs through every shared exercise. Each class has a class representative, and the third-year Hero Course includes the Big Three, the students the academy counts as its strongest.
